name: Beard transplant

card.summary: Follicular unit grafts moved to the jaw and cheeks to fill patchy or absent facial hair; described in surgical reviews as a refined procedure, with outcome data limited to surgeon-reported series.
card.aka: facial hair transplant, beard hair restoration
card.note: Published evidence is surgeon-authored reviews and experience reports; no controlled trials were found.

quick.overview:
A beard transplant moves hair follicles, usually from the scalp, into areas of the face where beard growth is sparse or absent. It is a branch of hair restoration surgery and uses the same graft-based techniques as scalp transplantation, with small recipient sites angled to match natural beard direction.

Surgical reviews describe it as having grown in importance because of its natural-looking results. The available literature consists mainly of surgeon experience, such as one review reporting more than 700 primary beard transplants by a single author, rather than controlled studies.
quick.mechanism: Grafts containing one or two hairs are harvested, trimmed to a minimal cuff of skin and placed into tiny recipient sites using the smallest possible blades, with angulation and design chosen to look natural. Transplanted hair is expected to keep the traits of its donor area.
quick.risks: Reviews discuss reparative procedures for poor results, and general hair-transplant risks such as swelling, scarring and infection apply. A looksmaxxing-specific evidence base is absent; no forum material is cited here.

lead: Beard transplantation is the surgical relocation of hair follicles, usually taken from the scalp, to areas of the face where facial hair is thin, patchy or absent. It sits within hair restoration surgery alongside eyebrow, sideburn and eyelash transplantation [1][2][5].

Men use it to fill gaps in a beard, to add density along the cheeks and jawline, or to create a beard where little grows, giving a fuller and more defined lower face. Because transplanted hair keeps the growth characteristics of its donor site, the grafts continue to grow once they take, and can be trimmed and styled like the rest of the beard [5].

A 2024 review by a surgeon with experience of more than 700 primary beard transplants and many repair procedures states that restoring the beard area has become an important part of hair restoration surgery because of its natural-appearing results, and emphasizes careful graft dissection, acute angulation of recipient sites and aesthetic design [1]. A 2013 review similarly describes beards, goatees and sideburns as popular procedures whose results can be outstanding [2].
The published evidence consists of expert reviews and personal series. No controlled trials of beard transplantation were found.
infobox: Scalp (FUE or FUT); body hair is sometimes used [3][5]
About US$3,000-7,000 for partial and $15,000 or more for full beards, per Grokipedia [3]
Around three to four months, fuller at about a year, per Grokipedia [3]

paras: According to a 2024 review, key aesthetic steps include dissecting grafts so that one- and two-hair grafts have a minimal cuff of surrounding skin, making recipient sites with the smallest possible blades at acute angles and appropriate direction, and planning the beard's design [1]. The review also covers beard-to-scalp hair restoration, in which beard hair is used as a donor source for the scalp [1].

Wikipedia's article on hair transplantation explains that hair grows naturally in groups of one to four hairs, so modern procedures move follicular units in their natural groupings, and that donor hair is harvested either by strip excision (FUT) or by follicular unit extraction (FUE) using 0.6-1.0 mm punches under local anaesthesia [5]. FUE leaves small dot-like scars and has a shorter recovery than FUT, which leaves a thin linear donor scar [5]. The article adds that body-hair transplantation requires FUE and an experienced surgeon, and that texture and growth-rate differences must be considered [5].

Grokipedia, an AI-generated source treated with caution, says follicles are typically taken from the scalp by FUE or FUT, that body hair can be a less reliable donor, and that results begin around three to four months with fuller results at about a year [3].

Facial-hair grafting grew out of the broader history of hair transplantation. Wikipedia reports that Japanese surgeons in the 1930s used small follicular-unit-style grafts mainly for eyebrows and eyelashes, that in the late 1950s New York dermatologist Norman Orentreich showed transplanted hair keeps the growth pattern of its donor site, and that in the 1980s strip excision with many small grafts replaced early plug techniques [5]. FDA approval of robotic harvesting devices followed in 2009 (NeoGraft) and 2011 (ARTAS) [5].

The reviews describe natural-looking results as achievable by an experienced surgeon [1][2]. They discuss repair of poorly executed work, indicating that results depend on technique [1]. Grokipedia lists swelling, scarring and infection among risks, as with scalp transplantation [3]. Wikipedia notes that temporary thinning (shock loss) is common after hair transplantation generally, and that bleeding-related medications, alcohol and smoking can reduce graft survival [5]. No published trial compares outcomes across techniques or clinics.

Prices vary with the number of grafts. Wikipedia reports average costs per graft in hair transplantation from about US$1.07 in Turkey to US$7.00 in Canada, which affects where patients choose to travel [5]. A 2014 news piece shared on Hacker News described a rise in demand for facial hair transplants among men seeking fuller beards [6].

On T Nation, beard growth is discussed mainly in relation to genetics and hormones; one poster says a man who is genetically not very hairy will not grow a full beard however high his testosterone, adding that hair transplants are an option if all else fails [7].
No studies found of beard transplantation beyond surgeon-reported reviews [1][2]. A registered trial of follicular unit extraction for alopecic scars (not specific to the beard) exists [4].

claims.claim: Testosterone level alone decides whether a man can grow a full beard
claims.believers: A T Nation member says that a genetically low-hair man will not grow a full beard however much testosterone he has, and that hair transplants are the fallback [7].
claims.experts: Surgical reviews present transplantation as a way to restore beard areas with natural-appearing results [1][2].

claims.claim: Beard transplants look natural when done by an experienced surgeon
claims.experts: The reviews note repair procedures are also needed after poorly executed work, and no controlled trials compare outcomes [1].

chain: Follicles are harvested from the scalp (or sometimes the body)
Grafts are placed individually along the beard area
Transplanted hairs grow as a fuller, denser beard
angle.text: A surgeon moves individual follicular-unit grafts into patchy or bare areas of the cheeks, chin, jawline or moustache and plans the angle and direction so the beard looks natural. Patients seek it for density and shape that grooming and topicals have not provided.
